instruction.text: Drag the bricks to complete Hadrian’s Wall.

atoms.b: Growing tired of the Picts, the Roman ((++emperor pharaoh)), Hadrian, decided to stop expanding north and built a wall instead.
Hadrian’s Wall was built 73 miles across modern-day ((++England France)) to mark and protect the northern edge of Roman Britain.
The construction began in AD ((++122 2022)) and took 6 years and over 15,000 soldiers to build.

instruction.text: Select the three materials that were used to build Hadrian’s Wall.

feedback.finish: Although stone was preferred, Romans sometimes used turf bricks made from earth and grass.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: After Emperor Hadrian’s death, his adopted son Antoninus Pius became emperor and constructed a second wall. The building of the Antonine Wall started in around AD 142.
Like Hadrian’s Wall, the Antonine Wall was built to protect Roman land, this time with the border pushed further north.
After repeated attacks by local tribes, the Antonine Wall was abandoned after just 20 years. Despite several attempts to retake Caledonia, the Romans had to retreat back to Hadrian’s Wall.

atoms.a: Where was the Antonine Wall built compared to Hadrian’s Wall?
Why did the Romans abandon the Antonine Wall?
b: They expanded their frontier further north into Caledonia.
++They were attacked by the Picts and had to withdraw from Caledonia.
The Picts allied with Rome, making the wall unnecessary.

text: Large stretches of both walls still stand today, forming footpaths that run across the width of the UK!
